rv.q: Yet it’s at least as frustrating as it is inspiring.
It’s just a shame that the something they’re doing is this.
It's wall-to-wall with tunes that will make you want to dust of your denims and, like Jemma, come to realise that for all its flaws, Live Aid is an event well worth celebrating.
It is a truth not sufficiently acknowledged that something can be not very good but also hugely enjoyable at the same time.
No matter how old you are, there is something for everyone in this inspiring and immaculate musical.
It’s uplifting, emotional and inspiring — a reminder of what can happen when music brings people together.
This is a show that is there to do good, and with a diverse cast (race, gender) it highlights the universal power of a movement.
Craige Els is impeccable, ranting and raving, full of angst and anger and never taking no for an answer.

cn.t: Critics find this Live Aid musical an enjoyable nostalgia trip with powerful performances and iconic songs, though some fault it for being shallow and earnest. A crowd-pleasing spectacle that entertains despite its narrative flaws.
